title: 1954 AHSME Problem 19
statement: If the three points of contact of a circle inscribed in a triangle are joined, the angles of the resulting triangle:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: are always one obtuse angle and two unequal acute angles

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: are always one obtuse angle and two equal acute angles

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: are always unequal to each other

solutions.text:
The radii to two adjacent tangency points are perpendicular to the corresponding sides. The central angle between those radii is \(180^\circ-A.\) The relevant angle of the contact triangle is half the intercepted arc, giving \[ 90^\circ-\frac A2. \] The other two angles are \(90^\circ-\frac{B}{2}\) and \(90^\circ-\frac{C}{2}.\) Since every triangle angle lies strictly between \(0^\circ\) and \(180^\circ,\) all three are acute.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Join the incenter to two adjacent points of tangency
The angle of the contact triangle opposite vertex angle \(A\) is \(90^\circ-\frac{A}{2}\)
